sources.title: Landing page mock: one design language
sources.description: One visual language connects the upload panel, example cards and pricing table.

sections.heading: Decision and rationale
sections.text: One visual language connects the upload panel, example cards and pricing table. Cream backgrounds and restrained cyan highlights keep the file drop target prominent. The mock removes the competing illustration so publishing is the first action visitors see. Navigation uses the same spacing scale as the upload controls, and every primary button has one consistent label.

sections.heading: Operational checks
sections.text: The mobile layout places the drop target before explanatory copy. Keyboard users can choose a file with the same visible control. Upload progress stays inside the panel and becomes a shareable link when publication finishes. Error text names the rejected file and tells the visitor which formats the publisher accepts.

sources.title: Artfct vs a shared drive — draft
sources.description: A shared drive stores files but does not make their contents available inside every assistant.

sections.heading: Decision and rationale
sections.text: A shared drive stores files but does not make their contents available inside every assistant. Artfct publishes durable documents that authenticated AI tools can search by meaning. The distinction matters when an analyst saves a report and another teammate needs its conclusion in a different chat. Folder names alone do not convey the evidence contained in a report.

sections.heading: Operational checks
sections.text: Team membership controls access to shared work. A search returns a source link and a relevant excerpt instead of requiring a teammate to remember a filename. The document remains owned by the company when someone changes AI vendors. People still decide what to publish; private conversations are not copied into the workspace automatically.

sources.title: Why your AI tools cannot see each other's work — draft
sources.description: An assistant conversation is local to its vendor and session.

sections.heading: Decision and rationale
sections.text: An assistant conversation is local to its vendor and session. A report created in one chat is invisible to another assistant unless someone transfers it. This makes teams rebuild analysis that already exists. Publishing the report once gives other connected tools a stable source to retrieve, so their next answer can start from the completed work.

sections.heading: Operational checks
sections.text: The shared knowledge base preserves the report and its source rather than attempting to synchronize hidden conversation history. A teammate asks in natural language, retrieves the published document and opens the evidence. The author chooses which outputs become team knowledge. Nothing requires both teammates to use the same assistant or to paste the report into each new chat.

sources.title: How we stopped our AI tools from contradicting each other
sources.description: Conflicting answers came from stale local copies of the launch brief.

sections.heading: Decision and rationale
sections.text: Conflicting answers came from stale local copies of the launch brief. The team published one approved brief with a visible revision history and asked every assistant to consult it. Engineers and marketers could then compare the source date before accepting a proposed deadline. A stable document link replaced several screenshots of chat answers that no longer agreed.

sections.heading: Operational checks
sections.text: The review process assigns an owner to each approved brief. When the deadline changes, that owner publishes a new version and leaves the earlier version available for audit. Agents should cite the consulted version. A common footer says our AI makes, remembered, but that slogan contains no evidence about the deadline or approval process.

sources.title: Greenhouse recruiting connector rollout
sources.description: The Greenhouse connector imports hiring pipeline stages into a recruiting dashboard.

sections.heading: Decision and rationale
sections.text: The Greenhouse connector imports hiring pipeline stages into a recruiting dashboard. It reads candidate counts after the recruiting administrator grants the integration access. The rollout concerns applicant tracking, not agriculture. The first report groups openings by department and displays the number of applicants waiting for an interview scheduling decision.

sections.heading: Operational checks
sections.text: Recruiters validate stage mappings in a sandbox before enabling the scheduled import. A missing stage identifier pauses that opening rather than assigning applicants to a guessed stage. The connector does not write interview feedback or change candidate status. Audit events record the import time and the administrative connection used for each run.

sources.title: Invoice reconciliation exception policy
sources.description: Invoice reconciliation matches purchase order numbers before comparing totals.

sections.heading: Decision and rationale
sections.text: Invoice reconciliation matches purchase order numbers before comparing totals. Differences below two dollars go to the rounding queue; larger differences require a finance reviewer. The service records both original amounts instead of modifying the imported invoice. This preserves the supplier evidence and lets reviewers distinguish a currency conversion problem from a rounding discrepancy.

sections.heading: Operational checks
sections.text: A duplicate supplier invoice is quarantined using the supplier account and invoice number together. Re-running the daily import keeps the existing exception record and adds an audit entry. Reviewers resolve exceptions only after checking the purchase order and receipt. Approved resolutions retain a link to the original supplier file and the reviewer decision.

sources.title: Queue retry policy for supplier imports
sources.description: Failed supplier imports retry after one minute, five minutes and thirty minutes.

sections.heading: Decision and rationale
sections.text: Failed supplier imports retry after one minute, five minutes and thirty minutes. A validation error never retries because replaying malformed data cannot fix it. Network interruptions are retryable only when the import key is stable. The job stores a supplier batch identifier before contacting the remote service so a replay can identify an already accepted batch.

sections.heading: Operational checks
sections.text: After the final attempt the queue records the failed batch and alerts the operations owner. The operator checks remote acceptance before manually resubmitting. Queue visibility timeouts exceed the maximum job duration to prevent two workers importing the same batch concurrently. Failure diagnostics contain batch keys and response codes, but omit credentials and supplier contact details.

sources.title: Resolving ERR_ARTIFACT_VERSION_STALE
sources.description: ERR_ARTIFACT_VERSION_STALE means the requested version is older than the revision required by the caller.

sections.heading: Decision and rationale
sections.text: ERR_ARTIFACT_VERSION_STALE means the requested version is older than the revision required by the caller. The client should fetch the artifact metadata, compare the current version and ask for the expected revision explicitly. It must not silently substitute a newer report when an audit task needs the historical evidence used in an earlier decision.

sections.heading: Operational checks
sections.text: A stale-version warning differs from a missing artifact. The document may still exist and remain readable to an authorized teammate. Operators check the version number alongside the artifact identifier and workspace slug. A migration that drops version metadata can cause this warning even when the content bytes are present; rebuilding the version mapping resolves that inconsistency.

sources.title: Service token rotation checklist
sources.description: Token rotation first creates a replacement credential with the same scopes.

sections.heading: Decision and rationale
sections.text: Token rotation first creates a replacement credential with the same scopes. The operator deploys consumers with the replacement, verifies successful calls and only then revokes the old credential. Revoking before consumer rollout creates a preventable outage. Readiness checks must exercise an authorized operation rather than merely confirming a configuration value is nonempty.

sections.heading: Operational checks
sections.text: Every service owner records the rotation window and the consumers they verified. Diagnostics show credential identifiers rather than secret values. A rollback may restore application code but must not restore a revoked secret. If the replacement fails, operators investigate its scopes and destination before issuing another credential or expanding access.

sources.title: Research document retention schedule
sources.description: Research drafts expire after ninety days unless an owner marks them for continued use.

sections.heading: Decision and rationale
sections.text: Research drafts expire after ninety days unless an owner marks them for continued use. Approved decision records remain for seven years. A legal hold suspends deletion regardless of the normal expiry date. The retention sweep reports held documents separately so operators do not mistake a skipped deletion for a failed storage operation.

sections.heading: Operational checks
sections.text: The policy covers published documents and every retained version. Collection membership does not extend a draft expiry by itself. Owners receive a reminder before the expiry window and may promote a draft to an approved record after review. Deletion writes an audit event identifying the policy applied, while the deleted body is excluded from future retrieval.

sources.title: Cache invalidation after price updates
sources.description: Price updates invalidate product summary keys after the database transaction commits.

sections.heading: Decision and rationale
sections.text: Price updates invalidate product summary keys after the database transaction commits. A rollback leaves the old cache valid because no new price became visible. The invalidation event includes the product identifier and pricing region. Consumers recompute only the affected region rather than flushing every catalog key whenever one price changes.

sections.heading: Operational checks
sections.text: Read requests may serve an existing value while a background refresh runs for noncritical catalog descriptions. Checkout totals always read the committed price and do not use the descriptive cache. Tests cover a committed update, a rolled-back update and two regional prices with the same product identifier. Cache diagnostics expose key names without customer order data.

sections.heading: Inventory
sections.text: Inventory all readers before the timezone migration begins. Record the jobs, exports and screens that use the original customer fields. A background import may depend on the same field even when the user interface no longer displays it.

sections.heading: Validation
sections.text: Validate account timezone names against the supported timezone database. Invalid names go to a review queue instead of receiving the server default. Analysts compare a sample of account timestamps before and after conversion to catch daylight saving errors.

sections.heading: Monitoring
sections.text: Monitor database replication during each backfill batch. Progress reports include batch duration, committed rows and the oldest unprocessed account. A slow batch is investigated before increasing concurrency; reducing query size can be safer than adding more workers.

sections.heading: Decision and rationale
sections.text: The customer table migration adds nullable timezone fields before any application code reads them. A backfill fills known account timezones in small batches. The application then reads the new fields with a documented fallback. Removing the old field comes in a later release after the backfill and consumer verification finish.

sections.heading: Operational checks
sections.text: Migration progress is measured with the number of remaining null values and the oldest unprocessed account. Operators pause the backfill if replication lag exceeds ten seconds. Failed batches resume from their last committed cursor. A rollback of reader code is safe during the expansion stage because the original account fields are still present.

sources.title: Checkout outage postmortem
sources.description: The checkout outage followed an unbounded retry loop against the tax service.

sections.heading: Decision and rationale
sections.text: The checkout outage followed an unbounded retry loop against the tax service. Each timeout started another request while the earlier request was still active. Connection pools filled within three minutes. The mitigation disabled retries temporarily and returned a clear unavailable message while the tax service recovered. No orders were accepted without a valid tax calculation.

sections.heading: Operational checks
sections.text: The corrective change sets a shared request deadline and permits one bounded retry for transient transport failures. Load testing uses a deliberately slow tax service to check that concurrent requests stay below the pool limit. Alerts now compare active outbound calls with completed orders rather than treating high request volume as successful throughput.

sources.title: Navigation accessibility review
sources.description: The navigation review found that the mobile menu trapped focus after it closed.

sections.heading: Decision and rationale
sections.text: The navigation review found that the mobile menu trapped focus after it closed. Closing the menu now returns focus to its trigger. Escape dismisses the menu and tab order follows the visible links. The desktop navigation keeps the same labels and destinations, so keyboard and screen reader users do not encounter a second information structure.

sections.heading: Operational checks
sections.text: The reviewer checks the menu at narrow widths and at two hundred percent zoom. Interactive targets remain large enough for touch input, and active link state has a text cue in addition to color. Regression checks include opening with the keyboard, following a link and closing without navigation. Decorative icons are excluded from accessible link names.

sources.title: Renewal risk scorecard
sources.description: The renewal scorecard combines days since the last active user session, unresolved support cases and the account renewal date.

sections.heading: Decision and rationale
sections.text: The renewal scorecard combines days since the last active user session, unresolved support cases and the account renewal date. A high score prioritizes human review rather than automatically cancelling the subscription. Analysts inspect each contributing signal because a holiday or planned maintenance period can explain a temporary reduction in activity.

sections.heading: Operational checks
sections.text: Customer success reviews the scorecard every Monday and records the outreach owner. The report excludes accounts that renewed before the snapshot cutoff. Historical snapshots retain their original inputs so a later support resolution does not rewrite the reason an account was flagged. A separate field records whether the outreach improved renewal confidence.

sources.title: Warehouse late-arrival handling
sources.description: Late-arriving warehouse events are assigned to their original event day rather than the ingestion day.

sections.heading: Decision and rationale
sections.text: Late-arriving warehouse events are assigned to their original event day rather than the ingestion day. The nightly job recalculates affected daily totals for a seven-day correction window. Events older than the window enter an exception table for analyst review. This avoids silently shifting revenue into the wrong reporting period when a supplier sends a delayed batch.

sections.heading: Operational checks
sections.text: Each correction carries the upstream event identifier, the old total and the revised total. Dashboards mark corrected days so viewers can explain changes between snapshots. Duplicate events share one deduplication key across normal and correction paths. The analyst may authorize an older correction after checking the monthly close status and communicating its reporting impact.

sources.title: Blue green deployment rollback procedure
sources.description: A blue green rollout first routes ten percent of requests to the candidate.

sections.heading: Decision and rationale
sections.text: A blue green rollout first routes ten percent of requests to the candidate. Operators compare error rate and latency with the existing deployment for fifteen minutes. A doubled error rate triggers rollback. The traffic switch retains the old environment until the observation window finishes, allowing a fast reversal without rebuilding a container image.

sections.heading: Operational checks
sections.text: Database expansion migrations must be compatible with both deployments during the observation window. A rollback changes routing and application code but does not undo accepted customer writes. Operators record the candidate deployment identifier and the point when traffic changed. Health probes include a database read and one authenticated application request to detect partial failures.

sources.title: Interactive capacity planning report
sources.description: The capacity report reserves thirty percent headroom above measured peak load.

sections.heading: Decision and rationale
sections.text: The capacity report reserves thirty percent headroom above measured peak load. The projection uses the busiest fifteen-minute interval rather than an average day. Operators can adjust the growth estimate in the browser, but the published baseline preserves the measured load and planning assumptions. This avoids presenting a reader edited scenario as an approved capacity commitment.

sections.heading: Operational checks
sections.text: At the projected load the report recommends adding two queue workers before increasing database size. Queue depth is the current bottleneck and the database remains below its tested saturation point. The owner reviews projections after a major customer launch. This page renders its substantive report with JavaScript, so a static title extraction cannot establish indexing readiness.

sources.title: Vendor onboarding control matrix
sources.description: Vendor onboarding requires a signed data processing agreement before transferring customer records.

sections.heading: Decision and rationale
sections.text: Vendor onboarding requires a signed data processing agreement before transferring customer records. The procurement owner verifies contract scope and records the security review result. A sandbox trial may proceed with fictional data while the review is pending. Production integration remains disabled until procurement and security approve the intended processing purpose.

sections.heading: Operational checks
sections.text: The onboarding matrix tracks contract review, security review and operational ownership separately. A completed contract does not imply a completed security assessment. The operations owner tests failure handling and credential rotation before launch. Evidence links remain attached to each approval so the next reviewer can see exactly which version of the assessment supported the decision.

sources.description: The handoff library contains separate runbooks for deploys, incident escalation and supplier imports.

sections.heading: Decision and rationale
sections.text: The handoff library contains separate runbooks for deploys, incident escalation and supplier imports. The incident runbook pages the primary responder after five minutes without acknowledgement. If that responder remains unavailable, the secondary receives the alert.
